THE PUBLIC-SERVICE CHALLENGE

What the model already knows

A general model can explain what permit renewal usually means and help write a clear response.

What the institution knows

The local authority knows which form applies, which proof it accepts and who publishes a change.

What the user needs

A reliable answer for this jurisdiction, with enough evidence to check or challenge it.

03 / 43
Pause on the distinction between a fluent, plausible explanation and an answer that applies to a particular jurisdiction today. A general model can help phrase an answer, but local requirements need to come from the institution’s maintained sources. If the policy changes, the knowledge and publication process must carry that change into the service. This is the first design question to carry forward: who owns the source and how does a change reach users?

11 / 43
Tell the lifecycle in order: an authorised user uploads a file, it remains Pending, and an administrator triggers Ingest from the dashboard or API. The configured pipeline scans uploads with ClamAV when enabled, extracts supported formats using the available parser, splits the text into chunks, creates embeddings and stores the searchable result. Docling handles supported formats such as PDF and DOCX in the reference setup. Use the highlighted overlap to explain why adjacent chunks can share context; smaller chunks may improve focus but can also split context, so size and overlap need evaluation against real documents. These are deployment settings rather than per-question choices. If chunking or the embedding model changes, re-ingest affected files and check retrieval again. The sample guide and chunks are fictional.

What runs inside GENIE.AI?

AN ITU-INITIATED FRAMEWORK · APACHE 2.0 CODE LICENCE

Web & mobile

Vue 3 powers the web client. Flutter powers the Android and iOS clients.

Application & identity

The Node.js and Express backend brokers requests. Keycloak handles sign-in and identity.

Knowledge

Docling parses documents. ArangoDB stores indexed knowledge, including vector and graph data.

AI services

OPEA ChatQnA orchestrates RAG. TEI serves embeddings and reranking. vLLM serves generation.

Observability

OpenTelemetry collects signals. Victoria stores them. Grafana visualises them when enabled.

Deployment

The application runs on Docker Compose, Docker Swarm or Kubernetes via Helm.

Architecture · Apache 2.0 licence

This is the documented reference stack, not a requirement to activate every optional component in every deployment. Compose, Swarm and Kubernetes also use different edge and operational components, which we will compare later. The Apache 2.0 licence applies to the framework code; model weights, datasets and third-party services can have separate terms that the institution must review.

How the answer is built

Hybrid retrieval combines meaning and exact wording.

BM25 search

Rank lexical matches, such as a form number or a precise procedure name. GENIE.AI fuses the vector and lexical rankings.

Vector search

Find passages with related meanings, such as “renew my permit” and “extend its validity”.

Graph expansion

Optional graph traversal adds related chunks. Candidate retrieval remains subject to the account’s available knowledge.

Hybrid retrieval · OKF access control
14 / 43
Use the renewal question to contrast two useful signals. Vector search can find semantically related language even when the wording differs; BM25 can surface exact terms such as a form name or procedure number. GENIE.AI combines the lexical and vector rankings, while optional graph expansion can add linked material. No single signal guarantees a correct answer: the retrieved passages still need to match the request and the user’s access. This sets up the separate question of how the candidate set is ranked.

OPEN KNOWLEDGE FORMAT · CONCEPTS, LINKS AND SERVING GRAPHS

Concepts

Each concept is a Markdown document with YAML frontmatter. It captures a distinct topic such as proof of address.

Relationships

Typed links connect concepts across the knowledge base. A stewardship team can review the content and its links.

Serving graph

Enable OKF and select OKF-only or hybrid retrieval to search published, ingested repositories as separate graphs.

OKF Studio · OKF access control · OKF configuration
19 / 43
Introduce OKF as a structured way to curate concepts and their typed relationships, with content stored in a versioned repository. Keep three actions distinct: editing a draft, publishing a version and making the resulting knowledge available for serving after ingestion. OKF is configurable and can be disabled; the existing free-form corpus remains a separate path. When OKF is enabled, the selected retrieval mode determines whether queries use the OKF serving graph alone or combine it with the legacy corpus. The benefit is governed structure and lifecycle visibility, not automatic correctness.

Use a changed requirement to show why knowledge ownership is an operating responsibility. Deployment and operations

Choose the app platform and the GPU placement separately.

Application platform

Docker Compose runs the app stack on one host. Docker Swarm can orchestrate it across nodes. Kubernetes uses the GENIE.AI Helm chart.

Model-serving placement

Model services can run alongside the app environment on suitable GPU hosts or behind a dedicated external GPU API. All three platforms can use that API.

Hosting on premises or in the cloud is a separate decision.

Compose guide · Swarm guide · Kubernetes and Helm · Deployment topologies
33 / 43
Separate two choices that are often conflated: the application platform determines how the main services are packaged and operated; model-serving placement determines where GPU-backed endpoints run. “External” in the GPU setting means outside the application deployment and does not mean public internet or third-party hosting. The endpoint can remain inside the institution’s own network. Ask which constraints—existing platform skills, data boundaries or hardware ownership—will shape each decision.

Compose guide · Swarm guide · Kubernetes and Helm
34 / 43
Read across each row and compare the application platform with the two GPU-placement options. Compose and Swarm use the dual-mode Compose configuration and can point to a dedicated node with GPU_NODE_HOST and the GPU API credential; they can also run local model services when the host and scheduling support them. Kubernetes uses the Helm chart: external mode takes the configured GPU host and service paths, while in-cluster mode uses the chart’s GPU workload configuration and documented NVIDIA device-plugin requirements. All three platforms support an external GPU API. Choosing that API does not dictate which app platform to use.

Make the operational dependency explicit: teams still need to secure the endpoint, monitor its capacity and availability, manage credentials and test network paths. The deployment diagrams show a placement pattern, not a claim that all services must run on one physical node.
